column3: The Hebrew says Shalmaneser “came up against him” and calls Hoshea his servant.
The Hebrew repeats “went up” for the advance through the land and to Samaria.
Other gods are described as feared rather than worshiped.
The prophetic mediation is twice expressed as “by the hand”.
The Hebrew speaks of following vanity and becoming vain, without an explicit noun “idols”. The testimonies are described as warnings.
The Hebrew says they made their sons and daughters pass through the fire and “sold themselves” to do evil.
The descendants are called the “seed” of Israel.
The Hebrew does not explicitly name the LORD as the subject of tearing Israel away.
The Hebrew repeats the LORD’s name and says the settlers did not fear Him.
The Hebrew repeats that the people do not know the custom of the God of the land at the end.
The commands to go and live are plural, while teaching is singular. “From there” does not explicitly name Samaria.
The Hebrew says the priest taught them to fear the LORD.
